transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

I'm coming in today because I've been struggling with eating really huge amounts of food all at once. It feels like I completely lose control during these times and just can't stop myself from eating.
After these episodes of eating, do you ever do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yes, I do. It's really embarrassing to admit, but I usually force myself to throw up right after, and then I'll fast or exercise for hours to try and make up for it. I just feel so desperate to prevent any weight gain after I lose control like that.
To help me understand your situation better, could you tell me your current height and weight, and whether you have recently lost a significant amount of weight?

I don't know my exact weight because I avoid the scale as much as possible; looking at it just makes me incredibly anxious. I think I'm about 5 feet 4 inches, but I'm not sure if I have lost any weight recently. I just feel extremely uncomfortable and unhappy with my current body size.
Even though you avoid the scale, has anyone—like a doctor, family member, or friend—expressed concern that you have become dangerously thin or underweight?
No, I haven't really had anyone express concern about me being dangerously thin or underweight. To be honest, no one has ever said anything like that to me.
If you had to estimate, do you think your current weight is below normal, about average, or above average for your height?
I definitely feel like my weight is above average and that I'm overweight. When I look in the mirror, I just see myself as being much larger than I should be.
Even though you avoid the scale, do you remember what your weight was the last time you were weighed, perhaps at a doctor's office?

I honestly don't remember the exact number from my last doctor's visit. Whenever I have to get weighed, I always turn around and ask the nurse not to tell me because I prefer not to know. I just couldn't bring myself to look at the scale.
Have you noticed any physical changes recently, such as feeling cold all the time, feeling dizzy or weak, or has your menstrual period stopped?
No, I haven't really noticed feeling particularly cold, dizzy, or weak lately. My period hasn't stopped either, so I don't think I am experiencing any of those physical changes.
Have you noticed your clothes becoming very loose, or have you had to buy much smaller clothing sizes recently?
No, I haven't really noticed my clothes becoming loose or fitting any differently. I haven't had to buy any smaller sizes, so I don't think they've changed.
On average, how many times a week do you experience these episodes of losing control with eating followed by purging or fasting, and how long has this been going on?
On average, these episodes of losing control followed by purging or fasting happen at least once a week. I've been struggling with this cycle for about a year and five months now.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were Anorexia Nervosa and Bulimia Nervosa. Based on the patient's reports of no significant weight loss, clothes not fitting looser, normal menses, and no concerns from others about being underweight, Anorexia Nervosa is ruled out. The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Bulimia Nervosa, including binge eating and compensatory behaviors (vomiting, fasting, excessive exercise) occurring at least once a week for over a year.
